title: Automated Blast-Radius & Projected Impact Analysis for Multi-Agent Worktree Concurrency
target_platform: macOS / Python 3.11+ / Git Worktrees & Coordination Flight Board
hypothesis: Augmenting mission manifests with native 'projected_impact' declarations and extending manage_coordination.py with an automated overlap matrix enables the flight board to automatically acquire exact target leases, surface disjoint parallel dispatches to incoming agents, and eliminate 100% of concurrent worktree merge conflicts without manual target path configuration.
falsification_criteria: An agent is able to check out a mission that silently conflicts with an active lease, manual --targets are still required at CLI checkout for registered missions, or collision detection overhead exceeds 500ms.
baseline_evidence: MISSION-026 established decentralized optimistic file leases and the flight board; however, target paths currently require manual agent declaration at checkout, introducing risk of under-locking or coarse-locking during parallel dispatches.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate to frontier model only if cross-repository AST import graph traversal is required.

evidence.details: Pre-registered. Old flow (no --targets, loaded from git at c48db6b6a): 284 of 284 genuinely overlapping random mission pairs checked out silently (100% silent conflicts); 3/3 RED tests failed. New flow (projected_impact in the manifest, conservative component-wise overlap, shared generated files excluded): 500 pairs, 0 false negatives, 284/284 overlaps blocked, 0 manual --targets needed, 15 false positives (6.9%). Latency: registry matrix+dispatch p95 5.6 ms; per-mission lease check p95 0.19 ms at 200 missions/20 leases; 200-mission matrix 175 ms. Real git, 60 branch pairs: 0 conflicts among 23 predicted-disjoint pairs; 0 unpredicted conflicts; verify flagged 20/20 planted undeclared edits with 0 false alarms. Live registry: suggest returns 3 mutually disjoint missions (031, 023, 030); 13 open missions can run in parallel. Boundary: index.jsonl conflicted in 60/60 merges (regenerated by every mission): flagged as regenerate_after_merge, not eliminated. Dogfooding verify: 1 of 33 files of this mission was outside its own declaration (test_relay.py, also declared by MISSION-032). Shipped: impact.py, manifest-driven checkout, matrix/suggest/verify, relay dispatchable line, manage_backlog validation, 20 backfilled declarations, 36 new tests.

lessons_learned: A lease with no locks can never conflict: manifest-declared impact (projected_impact) makes checkout lock exactly what a mission touches, and refusing an undeclared lock-free checkout closes the silent under-locking hole.

Conservative overlap with a leaf rule (a path with an extension has no children) gave 0 false negatives at a 6.9% false-positive rate; two wildcard components are assumed to match, a cheap head/tail refinement would cut the false positives further.

Declarations are only as good as verify: run manage_coordination.py verify before the PR; a mission's own manifest and shared generated files are implicitly allowed, everything else outside the declaration breaks the no-conflict guarantee.

The hypothesis claim of eliminating 100% of merge conflicts does not hold for files every mission regenerates (index.jsonl conflicted in 60/60 merges); they need regeneration at merge time (MISSION-034), not locks.

Fix the checkout side effect at its root: write the IN_PROGRESS marker into the new worktree's manifest copy, not the main tree. Matrix performance: normalise once per mission (1.29 s -> 0.2 s at 200 missions).

projected_impact.basis: Declared 2026-11-04 by claude-code (MISSION-031 backfill) from the mission's hypothesis; a mission always also edits its own manifest. Refine at checkout and confirm with `manage_coordination.py verify`.

related_missions.MISSION-052: CONSUMER: MISSION-052 uses impact declarations and `verify` to check four workers' edits.
